policy.mini_reason: The four lessons are the compact subject-specific delta outside the fixed workbench. They are designed to travel together with code.md/code-samples.md as four orthogonal relationship examples; splitting each into another mini would remove the semantic trace, explanatory tests or relationship-preserving native view that makes it useful.
policy.counting_rule: UTF-8 decoded characters including newlines in lesson source, metadata, trace, tests and native view; excludes generated Python bytecode and the fixed workbench/template/vendor layer.

totals.decision: A 290-character readability cost removes 134–154-character compound lines, names intermediate evidence, and records the previously missing tree learning target without deleting any model, trace, test or view behavior. Further token reduction was rejected where it would turn semantic packets into positional data, hide subject relationships, minify CSS/JavaScript, or teach unsupported shared view helpers.

removed_generated_artifacts.reason: These CPython .pyc caches were copied into generated flat samples and made the official code-sample contract fail. They are not author source and are reproducible by Python compilation.

samples.assessment: Natural inorder traversal remains independent of visualization code. lesson.js now records the previously omitted observable target: connect left—root—right recursion to the strictly increasing BST result. trace.py derives stable tree entities, recursive stack, visit additions and metrics from frames; tests verify order, structural preservation and one visit per node; render.js updates persistent SVG nodes, edges and visit-order DOM with semantic labels.
changes: Added the missing learningTarget metadata. This is allowed author metadata, matches the interaction gate and the other three samples, and does not create a workbench API or visible template chrome.

samples.relationship: coordinate wavefront and unweighted shortest path
samples.assessment: Learner source remains canonical deque BFS. trace.py exposes queue order, visited coordinates, distances, predecessor path, current/candidate roles and discovered changes. Tests independently verify endpoints, adjacency/open cells and optimal length. The persistent SVG preserves cell identity, wavefront, queue and final path.
changes: Removed visualTitle and visualKicker because the fixed v2 workbench never reads them and the native view already authors its own heading; retaining them would teach a nonexistent template API.
Named cellRole and pathSummary and split compound evidence assignments so status, accessible description and path evidence are readable without nested 145-character expressions.

samples.assessment: Learner source remains the conventional Levenshtein recurrence. trace.py exposes the prefix table, active cell, diagonal/delete/insert dependencies and cell writes. Tests separate known result, boundary initialization and transfer cases. The native view preserves stable cells, dependency spokes, recurrence and result evidence.
changes: Removed unused visualTitle and visualKicker metadata without removing the actual learningTarget.
Named first_row_initialized and first_column_initialized before boundary_ok, replacing one 134-character assertion while preserving the same rule-based test.

samples.relationship: recursive call stack and remainder invariant
samples.assessment: Learner source remains natural recursive gcd without visualization calls. trace.py reconstructs stable call identities, quotient/remainder state, base case and return phase. Tests verify the target result, zero base case and input symmetry. The SVG keeps persistent call rows and makes each Euclidean division visible as quotient and remainder lengths.
changes: Removed unused visualTitle and visualKicker metadata while retaining the explicit learningTarget.
Named remainderEnd, callDescription, curve and depthSummary and wrapped SVG attributes; the same text, geometry and DOM attributes are emitted without 125–154-character compound lines.

cross_sample_findings.intentional_local_repetition: list() and svgElement() remain tiny self-contained primitives inside independent sandboxed native views. A shared sample-only view library would violate the copyable author-layer contract and teach a second renderer API.

verification.name: orthogonal sample generator contract
verification.evidence: The first audit run exposed copied __pycache__ files; after deleting only those reproducible artifacts, the contract passed before and after source cleanup.

verification.name: generated flat browser checks
verification.evidence: Each lesson was freshly generated with --flat-output --vendor-mode symlink and its own check.py. All eight runs passed initial/active/final screenshots, execution, syntax/runtime error surfaces, timeout recovery, native-view sandbox, fixed layout, scaled stage/resize, keyboard Output sash and reduced motion.

verification.name: algorithm and trace static checks
verification.evidence: All 12 structured algorithm tests passed in isolated namespaces; every finalize packet was JSON-serializable with the expected tree, grid, table or call-stack state.

verification.name: source and native view syntax
verification.evidence: All learner/trace/test Python compiled, all four render.js files passed node --check, all native bodies satisfy the forbidden-element/CSP contract, and no postMessage/fetch/view-owned runtime was introduced.

verification.name: tree learning-target follow-up
verification.evidence: After adding the missing tree-traversal learningTarget, both generator/template contract suites passed and a freshly generated flat tree sample passed execution, error/timeout recovery, sandbox, fixed/scaled layout, keyboard and reduced-motion checks.

rejected_changes.change: Deduplicate list/svgElement/annotation styles through a shared sample library
rejected_changes.reason: Each author layer must remain independently copyable into a sandboxed native view; a shared helper would create a second renderer API and hidden dependency.

rejected_changes.change: Shorten semantic packet keys, node/cell identities or named test evidence
rejected_changes.reason: would reduce token count by making trace causality and rule evidence harder for an Agent to learn.

rejected_changes.change: Remove learningTarget, trace.py, tests.py or subject-specific accessibility descriptions
rejected_changes.reason: would save characters by deleting the learning contract rather than improving code quality.
the user explicitly defines these four template-external author layers as one jointly loadable reference set; another lossy tier would add selection complexity and remove orthogonal evidence.
